remediation:
GATE 2 ATTEMPT 1. Both defects accepted as correct findings; neither was contested.

DEFECT 1 - produto prestador picker restored to master's population.
Root cause: I collapsed a per-person predicate and a call-site filter into one helper. master had TWO different pools and I did not notice: ProductDialog got `people.filter(p => p.isCollaborator)` with NO status filter (master line 1200), while the wizard memo got `p.isCollaborator && p.status === 'active'` (master line 3880). My `collaboratorPool` baked `status === 'active'` in and was used at both, silently narrowing the produto picker.
Fix: replaced `collaboratorPool(people)` with the per-person predicate `isCollaboratorPerson(person)`, whose body is now character for character the API's derivation - `person.funcoes.some((funcao) => !funcao.isSystem)` vs `funcoes.some((funcao) => !funcao.isSystem)` in deriveBooleanMirrors - with no status component. The status filter moved back to the one call site that had it. Both call sites are now structurally identical to master with only `person.isCollaborator` -> `isCollaboratorPerson(person)` substituted, and the verifier had already proven that substitution population-identical (migration 0012's backfill is the exact inverse of deriveBooleanMirrors). Each call site carries a comment saying why it does or does not filter on status, so the asymmetry is no longer silent.
Regression test: `optimistic-row-guard.test.tsx` > new describe `the produto prestador pool` > `offers an inactive pessoa carrying a custom função, and never a vendedor`. It mounts the REAL app (real QueryClient, real hooks, mocked api), resolves a bootstrap holding an inactive pessoa with a custom função, an active pessoa with only `vendedor`, and an active pessoa with a custom função, then navigates to /cadastros/produtos, clicks Novo produto, adds a Prestadores de serviço row and reads the `Prestador 1` option list. This home was chosen deliberately: the defect is in the WIRING (which pool the app hands ProductDialog), so no ProductDialog-level test could ever see it, and this file's existing `an unsaved row is never offered to a picker` block is already exactly this shape.
RED OBSERVED: re-applying the narrowing (`.filter((p) => isCollaboratorPerson(p) && p.status === 'active')` on the ProductDialog prop) failed 1 of 10 with `expected [ 'Pessoa Persistida' ] to include 'Prestadora Inativa'`. Note the received array is non-empty, which is the positive control doing its job: the test distinguishes a NARROWED pool from an empty or broken one. Restored and confirmed byte-identical by sha256 before/after, then re-ran green at 10/10.

DEFECT 2 - CLAUDE.md corrected, and verified rather than assumed.
The old line claimed `collaboratorPool` is 'any active pessoa ... exactly how the API derives is_collaborator'. False on both counts: the API has no status component, and the equivalence failed on precisely the population defect 1 changed.
I verified the claim instead of assuming it, by printing both derivations side by side: API `funcoes.some((funcao) => !funcao.isSystem)` (service.ts:1079) and web `person.funcoes.some((funcao) => !funcao.isSystem)`. The predicate bodies are now character for character identical, so the equivalence is true as of this commit - and the new wording states the shared definition, names deriveBooleanMirrors, and says explicitly that NEITHER side considers status.
